sampling_model.design: Four mutually independent repeated-cross-section samples indexed by \(g\in\{C0,C1,T0,T1\}\).
sampling_model.units: Within cell \(g\), \(X_{g,1},\ldots,X_{g,n_g}\) are independent draws from \(P_g\), with \(n=\min_g n_g\) and \(n_g/n\to\rho_g\).
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment group is untreated at period zero and exposed at period one; the intrinsic torus changes-in-changes lemma identifies the no-treatment treated-post map from invertible production maps and two \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclically monotone graphs.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cell density is bounded between \(c\) and \(C\) on \(\mathbb T^2\), both nested Brenier Jacobians are uniformly elliptic, and the selected population lift branches remain \(\beta\)-separated from lattice boundaries and the squared-distance cut locus.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each cell density uses the order-\(s\) signed periodized KDE followed by clipping at \(c/2\) and mass renormalization. The half-open-cell lift selector returns \(\widehat a_p,\widehat\phi_p,\widehat a_T,\widehat\phi_T\) and uses a fixed measurable fallback off its regular domain. Covariance pilots are two-fold cross-fitted, include the harmonic translation score, and are evaluated by adjoint elliptic solves; \(n^{-1}I_{2J}\) is added before every block inversion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 29 proves a \(\sqrt{n/\log(1/h_n)}\) pointwise Gaussian limit with covariance \(I_2/(4\pi)\) only when source and target are uniform on \(\mathbb T^2\).
Theorem 3.2 differentiates a Brenier map along one smooth target-density curve through a linearized Monge--Ampere boundary problem.

Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 identify the multivariate changes-in-changes counterfactual law and map under cyclic comonotonicity, while the estimation section gives consistency rather than a sampling law.

Section 3, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 identify the gradient-Green contamination influence and its pole singularity; the abstract reports numerical stable-type fluctuations but the paper does not prove a shrinking-bandwidth nested empirical central limit theorem.
Theorems 2.4 and 2.10 give a weak functional limit and bootstrap for empirical Brenier potentials and fixed weighted contrasts, not pointwise gradients.
Theorems 2 and 6 give near-matching global \(L^2\) minimax rates for one smooth transport map through wavelet semi-dual estimation and a Fano lower bound.
Theorem 18 gives the \(\log n/n\) global squared-risk upper rate for a two-dimensional smooth density plug-in map without a matching logarithmic lower bound.
Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 validate a smoothed bootstrap uniform band for a one-dimensional quantile-represented transport map.

Theorems 2--4 and Corollary 2 derive efficient influence functions and root-\(n\) cross-fitted inference for scalar ATT and scalar distributional estimands under a distributional bridge in paired panel data.

body.tldr: An intrinsic flat-torus changes-in-changes lemma identifies the translation-aware displacement of a nested Brenier counterfactual from invertible production maps and two \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclically monotone graphs. A half-open-cell selector writes each regular equivariant lift as \(x+a_F+\nabla\phi_F(x)\), while an open branch-margin condition and a measurable fallback make the target and estimator total. The project derives the exact four-input derivative including its harmonic translation mode, proves a general-density critical-plane Gaussian law for a specified positive-normalized periodized-KDE plug-in at rate \(\sqrt{n/\log(1/h_n)}\) under \(1/[2(s-2)]\leq a_h<1/9\), retains all finite-bandwidth cross terms, estimates them by cross-fitted adjoint solves, calibrates ridge-regularized fixed-grid ellipses, and matches the \(\log(1/h_n)/n\) squared-risk scale by explicit Green-aligned product-Hellinger alternatives.

project_justification.gap: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC motivates cyclic-comonotone changes-in-changes in Euclidean outcome spaces but does not prove the intrinsic squared-geodesic torus identification lemma; SunTchetgenTchetgen2025DebiasedCiC gives orthogonal efficient inference for scalar ATT and scalar distributional effects under a distributional bridge, not for a bivariate Brenier-map displacement under cyclic comonotonicity; ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT proves the relevant smooth-map pointwise limit for \(d\geq3\) and only the uniform-to-uniform special case for \(d=2\); the 2026 Green-influence and potential-limit papers still do not establish a pointwise gradient law with a generated target.
project_justification.niche: In the critical plane, a Green gradient has logarithmically divergent variance, while nesting makes the same control noises enter the outer target through more than one path. This creates a distinct four-sample covariance and a nonregular local information problem.
project_justification.fill: An intrinsic torus identification lemma first turns the periodic model into a causal model. A translation-aware measurable lift separates the harmonic vector \(a_F\) from the mean-zero potential \(\phi_F\). The exact pulled-coordinate derivative then identifies one leading outer Green response to four weighted empirical processes, one smoother generated-target response, and a bounded harmonic translation response. A pole parametrix, an exponent-audited tame nonlinear expansion, cross-fitted adjoint covariance with asymptotically negligible deterministic ridge, and explicitly normalized annular Green alternatives yield a joint limit, total simultaneous inference, and a matched local minimax rate.

body.related_work: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC motivates the production-function and cyclic-comonotonicity structure in Euclidean outcome spaces and the Card--Krueger application. McCann2001PolarFactorization supplies existence and almost-everywhere uniqueness of squared-distance optimal maps from absolutely continuous laws on compact Riemannian manifolds. The intrinsic cost \(c_{\mathbb T}(x,y)=d_{\mathbb T^2}(x,y)^2/2\), torus changes-in-changes identification step, and translation-aware selection \(\widetilde F(x)=x+a_F+\nabla\phi_F(x)\) are new here: the Euclidean changes-in-changes theorem does not prove this transfer, and Euclidean cyclic monotonicity of an arbitrary periodic lift is not equated with \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclic monotonicity. SunTchetgenTchetgen2025DebiasedCiC develops Neyman-orthogonal, semiparametrically efficient inference for scalar ATT and scalar distributional effects in paired panel data under a distributional bridge. Its target and assumptions are strictly non-overlapping with the present fixed-grid bivariate Brenier-map displacement under cyclic comonotonicity: neither result subsumes the other. ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT supplies the periodized KDE and quantitative Monge--Ampere linearization, proves the uniform dimension-two special case, and explicitly leaves general variable coefficients open. GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization supplies the implicit-function treatment of a single smooth density path. The arXiv:2607.19080v1 abstract of GonzalezSanzShengWuAvellaMedina2026Influence reports numerical stable-type fluctuations, while Section 3, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 establish the Green contamination influence and its pole singularity; the paper does not prove the shrinking-bandwidth nested empirical central limit theorem studied here. GonzalezSanzMordantSheng2026PotentialFCLT supplies the adjoint representation for weak potential contrasts and explicitly does not cover map gradients. HutterRigollet2021Minimax and ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2024Plugin establish global one-map risk results; neither gives a critical pointwise four-cell local lower bound. PonnopratOkanoImaizumi2024UniformBand motivates simultaneous transport-map uncertainty in one dimension, while the present ellipse problem requires singular bivariate adjoints.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The decisive analytic risk is uniform control of the variable-coefficient pole after transformed KDE smoothing. Before broad proof development, evaluate one nonseparable smooth torus law with nonconstant \(f_{T0}/f_{C0}\) at bandwidths \(h,h/2,h/4,h/8\), refine the PDE mesh until discretization changes are negligible, compare each cellwise covariance increment with \(V(P)\), and separately track the generated-target and harmonic-translation remainders. A persistent slope discrepancy, a logarithmically divergent remainder, or nonvanishing normalized Green--harmonic cross-covariance invalidates the proposed spine. The local converse must separately verify the two-sided \(L^2\) logarithmic norm and \(C^s\) envelope for \(\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\), positivity and normalization of both displayed alternatives, constructive membership in the intrinsic torus cyclic-comonotone class, preservation of diffeomorphism, ellipticity, lift-branch, and cut-locus margins, the \(O(n^{-1/2})\) translation change, bounded product-Hellinger distance for the least-sampled cell, first-order Green separation, and negligibility of the nonlinear remainder. The cutoff \(\varepsilon_n=n^{-\eta}\) is independent of \(h_n\); substituting \(\varepsilon_n=h_n\) is not licensed.
body.honest_scope: The intrinsic torus identification lemma is a contribution: the Euclidean changes-in-changes paper motivates the model but does not establish a flat-torus specialization. The target uses the unique half-open-cell translation \(a_T\) and mean-zero potential \(\phi_T\); it does not impose zero flux. Population inner and outer maps are maintained a fixed positive distance from the lattice branch boundary and the squared-distance cut locus. The estimator uses the same selector with a measurable fallback whose probability is \(o(1)\) by uniform consistency. The theorem concerns a fixed separated grid, independent repeated cross sections, positive smooth torus densities, the polynomial window \(1/[2(s-2)]\leq a_h<1/9\), and uniformly elliptic maps; it is not a confidence band and does not cover paired panels, vanishing densities, growing grids, branch-crossing sequences, or raw discrete counts. The endpoint \(a_h=1/[2(s-2)]\) is included because the remaining factor \(1/\sqrt{\log n}\) makes the deterministic bias negligible, whereas \(a_h=1/9\) is excluded because the stochastic quadratic remainder retains a \(\sqrt{\log n}\) factor. The exact derivative includes the harmonic translation term, although its bounded score has vanishing normalized variance and Green cross-covariance. Raw empirical covariance blocks may be singular, so every finite-sample ellipse uses \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^{R}=\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}+n^{-1}I_{2J}\); its conditional critical value may equal zero, and its asymptotic equivalence follows from covariance consistency and uniform positive definiteness of \(V(P)\). Card--Krueger employment counts do not literally satisfy the smooth model, so the empirical target must be declared in advance as a smoothed exploratory estimand and reported with regularization sensitivity. The local minimax claim is over genuinely two-dimensional perturbations whose causal-class membership and lift-branch stability are witnessed constructively. When only the treated-post law is sampled and all laws are uniform, the result reduces to Proposition 29 of ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT; when all four cells are sampled equally, it yields the four-noise covariance \(I_2/\pi\).
